title: All the adversaries' opinions on the translate have been confuted; none of them can explain sin's propagation more safely or easily than we who defend the creation of souls
pass_a_gloss:
Article XV. That all the opinions on the translate have now been confuted; likewise that no one from that number can explain the propagation of sin more safely or more easily than we who defend the creation of souls.
1. Those who think the soul is from a translate and is not created and infused by God are bound to assert that the soul is either educed from the potency of the seed through the passive concurrence of matter, or produced by the father's soul without the concurrence of the seed's matter: for between these two no middle is given. The prior opinion was confuted by me in Arts. III and XII. The latter mode of speaking we can distribute and subdivide into four other modes: For if the father's soul without the concurrence of the seed's matter produces the child's soul, it either produces it from its whole substance, or from a part of its substance, or from a certain spiritual seed, or from nothing: the first mode I confuted in Art. XII; the second in Art. XIII; the third in Art. XIV; and the fourth in Art. XIII. Whence I conclude that no opinion on the translate is given that is not absurd and contradicting the principles of sound Philosophy.
2. But now it is to be shown that no one among the Traducians can explain the propagation of original sin more safely or more expeditiously than we who defend the creation of souls. Meisner's reason, even when so conceived and limited, is of little efficacy. For they say: If the soul is created and infused by God, original sin cannot be transfused into it from the parents, because an accident does not pass from subject into subject. But we showed above, in Arts. VI and VII, how the several parts of original sin are propagated without traduction of the soul: the first through natural generation as an hereditary right; the second negatively, through the lack of justice which parents cannot confer; the third through a virtual disposition in the seed, by means of the sympathy of body and soul. Therefore the creation of the soul does not abolish but best reconciles the propagation of sin.
3. On the contrary, the Traducians, while they will have the soul materially translated, fall into greater absurdities: for they either make the soul divisible and corruptible, or attribute to the parent a power of creating, or invent an inexplicable spiritual seed. Therefore it is safer and easier, with the Catholic Church and the sounder Philosophers, that the soul be created and infused by God, and original sin be propagated in the mode explained by us.
4. End of the Second Exercise. The Third Exercise follows, On Faith, Knowledge, etc.
pass_b_english: Article XV. All the adversaries' opinions on the translate have been confuted; none of them can explain sin's propagation more safely or easily than we who defend the creation of souls.

1. Those who hold the soul from a translate, not created and infused by God, must say either that it is educed from the seed's potency by matter's passive concurrence, or produced by the father's soul without the seed's matter — there is no middle. The first was confuted in Arts. III and XII. The second splits four ways: the father's soul produces the child's from its whole substance, or a part, or a spiritual seed, or nothing. I confuted the first in Art. XII, the second and the from-nothing case in Art. XIII, the spiritual seed in Art. XIV. So no traducian opinion stands that is not absurd and against sound philosophy.

2. No Traducian explains original sin's propagation more safely or easily than we who defend soul-creation. Meisner's argument, even limited, is weak. They say: if God creates and infuses the soul, original sin cannot pass into it, because an accident does not pass from subject to subject. But Arts. VI–VII showed how each part propagates without soul-traduction: the first by natural generation as hereditary right; the second negatively, by justice parents cannot confer; the third by a virtual disposition in the seed through body–soul sympathy. Soul-creation does not abolish sin's propagation — it best reconciles it.

3. Traducians who want the soul materially translated fall into worse absurdities: they make the soul divisible and corruptible, or give the parent creative power, or invent an inexplicable spiritual seed. Safer and easier, with the catholic church and the sounder philosophers: God creates and infuses the soul, and original sin propagates as we have explained.
4. End of the Second Exercise. The Third follows — On Faith, Knowledge, and related questions.
source_text:
ART. XV.
Confutatas jam esse omnes sententias de traduce; item neminem ex isto numero posse tutius aut facilius explicare peccati propagationem, quam nos qui animarum creationem defendimus.

1. Qui putant animam esse ex traduce, & a DEO non creari & infundi, illi necesse habent asserere animam aut educi ex potentia seminis per concursum passivum materiae, aut produci ab anima patris absque concursu materiae seminis: nam inter haec duo nullum datur medium. Prior sententia a me confutata est, art. 3. & 12. Posteriorum modum loquendi in quatuor alios dispesce ac subdividere possumus: Si enim anima patris sine concursu materiae seminis producit animam filii, vel producit eam ex tota sua substantia, vel ex parte suae substantiae, vel ex semine quodam spirituali, vel ex nihilo: primum modum confutavi art. 12.; secundum art. 13.; tertium art. 14.; et quartum art. 13. unde concludo, nullam dari sententiam de traduce quae non sit absurda & contradicens principiis sanae Philosophiae.

2. Jam vero ostendendum est, neminem ex Traduciariis posse tutius aut expeditius explicare peccati originalis propagationem quam nos qui animarum creationem defendimus. Meisneri ratio etiam sic concepta & limitata parum efficax est. Dicunt enim: Si anima a DEO creatur & infunditur, non potest peccatum originale in eam transfundi a parentibus, quia accidens non transit a subjecto in subjectum. At nos supra ostendimus, art. 6. & 7., quomodo singulae partes peccati originalis propagentur absque traductione animae: prima per naturalem generationem tanquam jus haereditarium; secunda negative, per carentiam justitiae quam parentes conferre nequeunt; tertia per dispositionem virtualem in semine, mediante sympathia corporis & animae. Quare creatio animae non tollit, sed optime conciliat, peccati propagationem.

3. Contra, Traduciarii, dum animam materialiter traduci volunt, in majora absurda incidunt: aut enim animam faciunt divisibilem & corruptibilem, aut parenti virtutem creandi attribuunt, aut semen spirituale inexplicabile fingunt. Quare tutius & facilius est, cum Ecclesia Catholica & sanioribus Philosophis, animam a DEO creari & infundi, & peccatum originale propagari modo a nobis explicato.

4. Finis Exercitationis Secundae. Sequitur Exercitatio Tertia, De Fide, Scientia, &c.
